title: Ring map quasi-finite at a prime (affine notion)
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map of finite type, i.e. $S$ is finitely generated as an $R$-algebra: there are $n\ge0$ and $s_1,\dots,s_n\in S$ such that the $R$-algebra homomorphism $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$, $x_i\mapsto s_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], is surjective. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, and let $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the fibre ring of $S$ over $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], with $j:S\to F$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. Let $\overline{\mathfrak q}\subset F$ be the prime ideal of $F$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$, i.e. the unique prime ideal of $F$ with $j^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$ (it exists and is unique by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection], since $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$). We say that $R\to S$ is *quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$* if $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is an isolated point of $\operatorname{Spec}(F)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], that is, the singleton $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in the Zariski topology of $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$.

Part (2) of 00PL (a quasi-finite ring map = of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime) is not used by any citer and is not stated here. proof.text: *The definition is well formed.* $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ is a prime ideal of $R$ (the preimage of a prime ideal under a ring map), so $R_{\mathfrak p}$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and the fibre ring $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $j$ are defined [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] (applied to $A=R$, $B=S$) says that $\mathfrak Q\mapsto j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$ is a bijection from the primes of $F$ onto the primes of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, so there is exactly one prime $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ of $F$ with $j^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$ (namely $\ker\psi_{\mathfrak q}$); no choice is made. $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is a point of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}(F)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and 'isolated' means that $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open. So 'quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$' is a property of the pair $(\varphi,\mathfrak q)$; the finite-type hypothesis only restricts the ring maps for which it is used (Stacks states it there because the equivalent conditions of 00PK need it).
